nodes.characterization_summary: High-resolution XPS spectra of Co 2p in Cr-CoxP show more electron-rich Co due to Cr doping.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution XPS spectra of Co 2p in Cr-CoxP.

nodes.characterization_summary: UPS confirms higher conductivity of Cr-CoxP with work function of 3.74 eV and valence band of 2.06 eV compared to CoxP.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ultraviolet photoelectron spectroscopy (UPS) measurement also confirms the higher conductivity of Cr-CoxP for the smaller work function of 3.74 eV and higher valence band of 2.06 eV than that of CoxP.

nodes.characterization_summary: DFT calculations show Cr doping lowers OER RDS energy barrier to 0.27 eV in Cr-CoxP from 0.47 eV in CoxP.
nodes.evidence_snippet: DFT calculations testify that Cr doping could accelerate the OER kinetics and enhance OER performances for the lower energy barrier of RDS of Cr-CoxP (0.27 eV) than that of CoxP (0.47 eV).

nodes.characterization_summary: NiIr-LDH shows Cdl of 8.09 mF cm^{-2}, higher than NiFe-LDH's 1.89 mF cm^{-2}, indicating more active sites.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Moreover, alloying Ir could bring about more active sites for NiIr-LDH Cdl of 8.09 mF cm^{-2} than that of NiFe-LDH Cdl of 1.89 mF cm^{-2}.
